newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan court hears Bhutto reinstatement plea.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan court hears Bhutto reinstatement plea.

text.p: Pakistan's Supreme Court on Monday began hearing ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto's challenge to her November 5 sacking by President Farooq Leghari.
But the court rejected Bhutto's request that her petition be heard by all of its 14 judges, a so-called full court, rather than the seven-judge bench assigned to the case.
Leghari, once a political ally of Bhutto, dissolved the National Assembly (lower house) and dismissed her three-year-old government on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
Bhutto filed a petition on November 13 asking the court to restore her government, just as it had reinstated that of her main rival, Nawaz Sharif, sacked in a similar way in 1993.
Bhutto told reporters accompanying British Prime Minister John Major on Sunday she was not optimistic that the assembly, and by extension her government, would be restored.

She said the court had delayed hearing her case for nine weeks, in contrast to its prompt handling of Sharif's petition after he was removed by then-president Ghulam Ishaq Khan. The court restored Sharif's government after 37 days.
Both presidents wielded a controversial amendment tacked on to the constitution by the late military ruler General Mohammad Zia-ul-Haq in 1985.
Bhutto's lawyer, Aitzaz Ahsan, told the court on Monday that a full court had heard similar appeals against the dismissals of governments in the past and the precedents should be followed.
Chief Justice Sajjad Ali Shah turned him down on the grounds that other litigants would suffer if a larger bench was formed.

Shah also turned down Ahsan's request that it expunge from the record what he called objectionable remarks about Bhutto in a petition filed on Leghari's behalf to counter her plea, though the chief justice invited him to make his request in writing.
In November the court asked Ahsan to remove what it said was objectionable criticism of the president in Bhutto's petition.
Shah has said the court will decide Bhutto's case before general elections set for February 3.
Leghari said on Sunday that the elections would be stopped if the court restored Bhutto's government, but said there was a strong case against this happening.
